correctness.rationale: For both published scalar update equations, solving the implicit stage gives the rational factor R(z,t)=1+z/(1-tz). Independent sampling gives the exact nth-power second-moment criterion. The pointwise supporting polynomial identity for g(t)=((1-t)/t)^2 yields the universal 12 Var(T) lower bound; dominated convergence or Fatou handles the stiff limit including atoms at zero. An explicitly mean-half two-point family tends to ratio 12. For two-point stages a and 1, multiplying the expectation defect by positive denominators and clearing (1-a)^2 yields the displayed strictly negative polynomial at p=a^2/(1-a)^2; affinity in p proves the whole safe interval, and the stiff limit proves necessity beyond. A standard-library exact polynomial checker matches both identities, and 309 rational tests confirm instances. The tests are corroboration, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The 2024 method demonstrates mean-square A-stability failure for uniform stages but leaves its distributional mechanism undetermined. A sharp universal variance penalty for the natural mean-stage-preserving class and a constructive necessary-and-sufficient two-point A-stability frontier resolve complementary design questions for that exact published numerical method. The family admits occasional individually expansive stages, so the result is not merely the standard deterministic theta>=1/2 criterion. It identifies a mathematically motivated accuracy-versus-stability tradeoff while explicitly disclaiming full nonlinear order claims.
